memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle and made forty silver bases to go under them - two bases for each frame, one under each projection. For the other side, the north side of the tabernacle, they made twenty frames and forty silver bases - two under each frame." - Exod 36:23-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Twenty frames on the south. Twenty on the north. Every single one resting on two silver bases sunk into the desert ground.

The frames were identical, but each had its own assigned position and its own foundation. No frame could hold up the tabernacle alone, and none was redundant. Remove one and there is a gap in the wall.

Paul's picture of the church says exactly this. God has placed the parts in the body, every one of them, just as He wanted them to be (1 Cor 12:18). Placed — not scattered randomly. Your position in the family of God is not an accident.

That answers two temptations at once. The temptation to feel unnecessary: if you were removed, there would be a gap. And the temptation to feel indispensable: there are thirty-nine other frames doing the same work.

Notice the silver bases. Every frame rested on something it did not produce for itself. We stand on grace we did not manufacture — for no one can lay any foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ (1 Cor 3:11).

Stand where God has placed you. Someone is counting on that gap being filled.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you know where God has placed you, or are you drifting?
2. Do you feel unnecessary? Who would notice the gap if you stepped away?
3. What foundation are you actually standing on?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for placing me deliberately. Help me stand faithfully where You have put me, resting on Christ alone. Amen.
